books.title: Headway Beginner 5th Edition

units.title: Unit 1: Hello!
units.grammar: am/is/are; my/your; This is …; How are you?
units.vocabulary: What's this in English?; Numbers 1-10; Plurals

lessons.title: What's your name?
lessons.content: Hello, I'm Leo. Hello, I'm Mara. Hello, I'm Nari. Grammar am/is, my/your. 1 Read and listen. Serena: Hello. I'm Serena. What's your name? Tom: My name's Tom. Serena: Hello, Tom. 2 Listen again and repeat. GRAMMAR SPOT I'm = I am, What's = What is, name's = name is. 3 Stand up and practise. Hello, I'm Serena. What's your name? My name's Tom.

lessons.title: Introductions - This is ...
lessons.content: 1 Read and listen. Serena: Tom, this is Carlos. Carlos, this is Tom. Tom: Hello, Carlos. Carlos: Hello, Tom. 2 Practise in groups of three. Nice to meet you. 3 Read and listen. Paul: Hello. My name's Paul Bartosz. Sarah: Hello, I'm Sarah Taylor. Nice to meet you. Paul: Nice to meet you, too. 4 Practise in pairs. Say your first name and surname.

lessons.title: How are you?
lessons.content: 1 Read and listen. Artur: Hi, Dinos. How are you? Dinos: Fine, thanks, Artur. And you? Artur: I'm OK, thanks. Check it 4 Complete the conversations. A: Hello. My name's Usha. What's your name? B: My name's Ben.

lessons.title: Everyday English - Good morning!
lessons.content: 1 Complete the conversations. A: Good morning! What a lovely day! B: Good morning! Yes, it is lovely! 2 Put the words in the correct order. How are you today? Fine, thanks. And you? Photos: morning greetings, coffee shop, car goodbye, bedtime. Listen and check. Practise the conversations.

lessons.title: Vocabulary - What's this in English?
lessons.content: 1 Write the words. Pictures: phone, photo, bike, house. an apple, a bus, a phone, a laptop, an umbrella, a bike, a house, a bag, a watch, a book, a photo, a sandwich. GRAMMAR SPOT a book, an apple, a watch, an umbrella.

lessons.content: 1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four, 5 five, 6 six, 7 seven, 8 eight, 9 nine, 10 ten. 3 Write the numbers. five books, three bikes, eight houses, four umbrellas, six photos, seven laptops, nine watches, ten apples, four sandwiches. GRAMMAR SPOT Singular: one book. Plural: two books.

lessons.title: She's from China
lessons.content: Countries: Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, England, Egypt, France, Italy, Japan, Spain, Russia, Turkey, the United States. Grammar he/she, his/her. His name's Antonio. He's from Italy. Her name's Nuwa. She's from China.

lessons.title: Practice - Cities and countries
lessons.content: Where's Venice? It's in Italy. Where's Moscow? It's in Russia. Student A and Student B photos and prompts for pairwork.

lessons.title: Reading and vocabulary - A holiday in New York
lessons.content: 1 Read and listen. This is a photo of Claude and Holly Duval from Montreal in Canada. They are on holiday in New York City. Holly is from Canada and Claude is from France. They are married. Holly is an architect. Her office is in the centre of Montreal. Claude is a doctor. His hospital is in the centre of Montreal, too. 2 Complete the sentences. 1 Holly is from Montreal in Canada. 2 She's an architect. 3 Her office is in the centre of Montreal. 4 Claude is from France. 5 He's a doctor in the centre of Montreal. 6 His hospital is in the centre of Montreal. 7 They are on holiday in New York. 8 They are married. 3 Complete the questions about Claude and Holly. Ask and answer with a partner. What's his name? What's her name? Where is her office? Where is he from? Where is his hospital? GRAMMAR SPOT Write is or are. You are a teacher. She is an architect. He is a doctor. They are from Montreal. Listen again and check. Practise the conversations. Go online for more grammar practice. Watch video about different cities and countries.

How old is he or she? I think he is about 26. I think she is 30. Listen and find out. Go online for more speaking practice.

lessons.title: Grammar reference and Wordlist - Unit 2
lessons.content: Grammar reference 2.1 Possessive adjectives: My name's Serena. What's your name? His name's Antonio. What's her name? his = possessive adjective (his name, his bike). he's = he is (He's Bruno. He's from Brazil. He's fine.) 2.2 Questions with question words: Where are you from? Where is she from? Where is he from? What's this in English? How old are you? I'm 27. How old is he? He's 18. How old is she? She's 12. 2.3 am/are/is: I am from England. I am a student. You are from England. You are a student. He is a student. She is a student. It is a laptop. It is in New York. They are in New York. They are married. Wordlist: amazing, architect, awful, beautiful, building, centre, city, country, doctor, fantastic, favourite, great, hamburger, hospital, map, married, office, on holiday, really good, too, view, weather, where, world, you're right. Countries: Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Egypt, England, France, Italy, Japan, Russia, Scotland, Spain, Turkey, the United Kingdom, the United States. Numbers 11-30: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty, twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-three, twenty-four, twenty-five, twenty-six, twenty-seven, twenty-eight, twenty-nine, thirty.

lessons.title: What's his job?
lessons.content: 1 Match the jobs and the photos. a teacher, a police officer, a taxi driver, a builder, a receptionist, a businessman, a nurse, an architect. Photos 1 to 8: 1 a businessman, 2 a teacher, 3 a police officer, 4 a taxi driver, 5 a builder, 6 a receptionist, 7 a nurse, 8 an architect. Listen and repeat. 2 Listen to the questions and answers and repeat. What's his job? He's a businessman. What's her job? She's an architect. 3 Look at the photos in exercise 1. lessons.title: Grammar - Negatives - he/she isn't plus Questions and answers
lessons.content: Grammar Negatives - he/she isn't. 1 Look at Sunil and Dana. Listen and repeat. Sunil: Teacher? Student? He isn't a teacher. He's a student. Dana: Nurse? Doctor? She isn't a nurse. She's a doctor. Questions and answers: Personal information. 1 Read about Adam. ID card: Surname: Clarke, First name: Adam, Country: England, Address: 37 Kings Street, Manchester, M12 4JB, Phone: 07700 955031, Age: 27, Job: Police Officer, Married: No. 2 Complete the questions and answers. 1 What's his surname? Clarke. 2 What's his first name? Adam. 3 Where's he from? England. 4 What's his address? 37 Kings Street, Manchester, M12 4JB. 5 What's his phone number? 07700 955031. 6 How old is he? He's 27. 7 What's his job? He's a police officer. 8 Is he married? No, he isn't. Listen and check. Practise the questions and answers with a partner. 3 Read and listen. Then listen again and repeat. Is Adam from Australia? No, he isn't. Is he from Canada? No, he isn't. Is he from England? Yes, he is. 4 Ask and answer the questions about Adam. 1 Is he from London, Oxford or Manchester? He's from Manchester. 2 Is he 19 or 27? He's 27. 3 Is he a teacher, doctor or police officer? He's a police officer. 4 Is he married? No, he isn't. Check it 5 Complete the sentences. 1 Adam isn't from Australia. He's from England. 2 His phone number isn't 07700 955032. It is 07700 955031. 3 He isn't 30. He is 27. 4 He isn't married. Watch a video about a woman called Paula Harrid.

lessons.title: Reading and listening - We're in Paris!
lessons.content: Reading and listening: We're in Paris! 1 Read the newspaper article about the football team, Scottish Rovers. Scottish Rovers in Paris: Scottish team in football final. The five-a-side football team, Scottish Rovers, are in the final in Paris. The team from Scotland are in the European final! They are all from Glasgow. Two of the girls, Shona and Gillian Robertson, are sisters. Shona is the captain of the team. 'We are so happy we're in Paris,' says Shona. 'Paris is beautiful and the Eiffel Tower is amazing!' The final is tomorrow and the girls are very excited. 'We're all fine,' says Gillian. 'We aren't nervous at all! It's fantastic to be in the final and it's great to be in Paris.' Today it's coffee time in a French café. Tomorrow they play Atlético Bilbao from Spain in the final! 2 Answer the questions. 1 Where are the girls? They are in Paris. 2 Is it the world final? No, it's the European final. 3 When is the final? Tomorrow. 4 Are they nervous or excited? They are excited. 3 Read about the team again. Correct the information. 1 Scottish Rovers are in Italy. They aren't in Italy. They're in France. 2 Shona is from England. She isn't from England. She's from Scotland. 3 Gillian is the captain. She isn't the captain. Shona is the captain. 4 The final is today. It isn't today. It's tomorrow. 5 They're in a hotel in Paris now. They aren't in a hotel. They're in a French café. Listen and check. Practise the lines. Interview with the team. 4 Listen to the interview with the girls and answer the questions. 1 Is it the team's first time in Paris? Yes, it is. 2 How old are Kate, Fiona and Emma? They are 19. 3 How old are the twins? They are 21. 4 Are the twins both married? No, they aren't. 5 Who is Tom? What's his job? Tom is their coach. He's a builder. 5 Look at audioscript on page 142. Read and listen to the interview. Roleplay 6 Work in groups of four. You are a sports team. What's your sport? What's the name of the team? What are your names? Where are you from? How old are you? What are your jobs? Ask and answer the questions with another group. Go online for more grammar practice.

lessons.title: Everyday English - Social expressions (1)
lessons.content: Everyday English: Social expressions (1). 1 Listen and look at the photos. 2 Complete the conversations with the words in the boxes. Photo 5: I: I'm sorry. I don't understand. Photo 6: K: Excuse me! Where are the toilets? L: They're over there. K: Thanks a lot. Listen again and check. 3 Work with a partner. Practise the conversations. Stand up and act out the conversations. Go online for more speaking practice.

lessons.title: Everyday English - On the phone
lessons.content: Everyday English: On the phone. 1 Look at the two business cards. What businesses are they for? 2 Listen and complete Conversation 1. Conversation 1: Operator: Good morning. Perez Taxis. Anita: Hello. Can I book a taxi for 11.15 this morning, please? Operator: Certainly. What's your name? Anita: It's Anita Jarvis. Operator: How do you spell your surname? Anita: J-A-R-V-I-S. Operator: Thank you. What's your address? Anita: 24 Avenida Balboa. Operator: And where do you want to go? Anita: Centro Santa Fe. Operator: And your phone number, please? Anita: 07700 123456. Operator: OK! Your taxi is booked for 11.15. Anita: Thank you very much. Listen again and check. Practise the conversation with your partner. 4 Listen and complete Conversation 2. Conversation 2: Lisa: Good afternoon. The Hotel Amira. Ian: Hello. Do you have a Family Deluxe room from 12-14 July? Lisa: Let me check. Yes, we have one family room left. Ian: Excellent. Can we have that? Lisa: Of course. And your name is, please? Ian: Ian McCaul. Lisa: McCaul ... Sorry. How do you spell your surname? Ian: M-C-C-A-U-L. Lisa: Thank you. And can I have your email address, please? Ian: It's ianmccaul@yippee.co.uk. Lisa: Thank you. I'll send you an email confirmation. Have a nice day. Ian: Thank you. 5 Listen again and check. Answer the questions. 1 What's the name of the hotel? The Hotel Amira. 2 What does Ian want? A Family Deluxe room from 12-14 July. 3 Is there a room free? Yes, there is one family room left. 4 What's Ian's email address? ianmccaul@yippee.co.uk. Email addresses: 6 Notice how we say email addresses. @ = at, . = dot, co, uk, ca. 7 Listen and complete the email addresses. 1 pam@btinternet.com, 2 harrylime@gmail.com, 3 paul@wanadoo.co.uk, 4 glennamiles@yahoo.ca. What's your email address? Tell a partner. Talking about you 8 Work with your partner. Practise the conversations with information about you. Go online for more speaking practice.

lessons.title: Grammar reference and Wordlist - Unit 4
lessons.content: Grammar reference 4.1 Possessive adjectives: This is my, your, his, her, our, their family, school, office. 4.2 Possessive 's': 's shows possession. This is John. This is his bike. -> This is John's bike. This is Marie. This is her car. -> This is Marie's car. Kelly and Tim are married. This is their son. -> This is Kelly and Tim's son. his house -> Noel's house, her name -> your wife's name, daughter -> Pam and Bob's daughter. 's is also the short form of is. he's = he is, she's = she is, it's = it is, who's = who is. 4.3 Common verbs: I, You, We, They like football. He, She likes football. I, You, We, They work in an office. He, She works in an office. Have is an irregular verb. I, You, We, They have a good job. He, She has a laptop. Wordlist: airport, a lot of, apartment, at home, boy, boyfriend, business card, businesswoman, charity, chef, children, class, classroom, college, dance, competition, dancing, dog, e-pal, famous, fan, fashion, friend, funny, hard, head teacher, important, interest, like, live, model, Northern Ireland, people, rich, school, schoolgirl, shop, spell, tennis, traditional, text, Turkish, university, work, young. The family: brother, daughter, father, husband, mother, parents, sister, son, wife.

lessons.title: This and that - This is my favourite
lessons.content: This and that: This is my favourite. 1 Look at the pictures. Complete the conversations with 'this' or 'that'. 1 A: This is my favourite teddy bear. B: Ahhh. What's his name? A: Teddy! 2 A: Wow! Who's that girl over there? B: It's my sister! A: She's beautiful! 3 A: Look at this new app! B: That's cool. What is it? A: It's a Premier League app. 4 A: How much is that bag? B: £85.99. A: That's expensive. 5 A: Look at that! B: It's awful! A: I think it's amazing. 6 A: Is this your coat? B: Yes. Thanks. A: My pleasure. 7 A: I like that ring. B: The gold one? A: No, the diamond one! 8 A: I like this wine. Where's it from? B: It's from England! A: Really? 9 A: This is for you, Daddy. B: For me? Why? A: Because it's your birthday! Silly! Listen and check. Practise the conversations. 2 Test the other students. Ask them questions about things in your classroom. 'What's this in English?' 'It's a newspaper.' 'What's that in English?' 'It's a door.'

lessons.title: Practice - I like you!
lessons.content: Practice: I like you! 1 Complete the sentences with you, her, it, us, them. 1 'Do you like pizza?' 'Yes, I love it.' 2 'Do you like cats?' 'No, I hate them.' 3 'Do you like me?' 'Yes, of course I like you.' 4 'Does your teacher teach you French?' 'No, she teaches us English!' 5 'Do you like your teacher?' 'Yes, we like her very much.' Listen and check. Questions and answers 2 Work with a partner. Ask and answer the questions. Why do you live in London? Because I like it. 1 Why do you live in London? 2 Why don't you eat tomatoes? 3 Why does Annie want to marry Peter? 4 Why do you eat so much chocolate? 5 Why does Dan always sit next to Sally? 6 Why don't you watch football? Listen and check. 3 What do you like? Ask and answer questions with a partner. Ask about football, golf, dogs, cats, Italian food, ice cream, pop music, coffee, Mondays, video games, Facebook, your neighbours. 'Do you like golf?' 'Yes, I love it!' 'No, I hate it!' 'Do you like cats?' 'Oh yes! I adore them!' 4 Match the questions and answers. 1 How do you come to school? c By bus. 2 What do you have for breakfast? h Toast and coffee. 3 Who's your favourite pop singer? d I don't have a favourite. 4 Where's your favourite pop singer? b In an office in the centre of town. 5 Why do you want to learn English? g Because it's an international language. 6 How much money do you have on you? e Not a lot. About £5. 7 What time do lessons start at your school? a They start at nine o'clock. 8 How many languages does your teacher speak? f Three. Listen and check. Practise the questions. Work with a partner. Ask and answer the questions about you. Go online for more grammar practice.

lessons.title: When was he born?
lessons.content: When was he born? 1 Listen and repeat. 1840 eighteen forty, 1996 nineteen ninety-six, 2005 two thousand and five, 2017 twenty seventeen. 2 Listen and underline the years you hear. 1 1696, 2 1960, 3 2014, 4 1799, 5 1945, 6 2017. 3 What year is it now? 2026. lessons.title: Vocabulary - Common verbs (2): have, do, go
lessons.content: Vocabulary: Common verbs (2): have, do, go. 1 Look at the words that go with have, do and go. 1 They have lunch at 1.00. 2 I always do my homework with my dad. 3 I go shopping with my friends on Saturday afternoons. 2 Write the words in the box next to the correct verb: have, do or go. shopping, my homework, lunch, a shower, the housework, on holiday, for a walk, some exercise, home, a good time, breakfast, to work. have: lunch, a shower, a good time, breakfast. do: my homework, the housework, some exercise. go: shopping, on holiday, for a walk, home, to work. 3 Write the past of have, do and go. have -> had, do -> did, go -> went. 4 Complete the sentences with went, had or did. 1 Yesterday I met my husband at one o'clock and we had lunch in a restaurant. 2 I hate doing housework, but last Sunday I did a lot because my house was a mess. 3 Yesterday was a lovely day so I went for a walk in the park. 4 I usually walk, but yesterday I went to work by bus. 5 On Saturday night we really had a good time. 6 I did my homework on the bus this morning. 7 The party wasn't very good so we went home early. Listen and check. lessons.title: Grammar reference and Wordlist - Unit 9
lessons.content: Grammar reference 9.1 was/were: Was and were are the past tense of am/are/is. Present: I am, He/She/It is, You/We/They are. Past: I was, He/She/It was, You/We/They were. Negative: I wasn't, He wasn't, You weren't, They weren't. Questions: Where were you yesterday? Was she at school? Yes, she was. No, she wasn't. We use was/were with born, not am/is/are. Where were you born? He was born in Russia. 9.2 Past Simple - irregular verbs: am/is/are -> was/were, buy -> bought, do -> did, go -> went, have -> had, make -> made, put -> put, run -> ran, see -> saw, sit -> sat. Wordlist: amazed, angry, astronaut, birthday, born, boxer, check, explorer, find, grandmother, grandson, housework, inventor, jackpot, last year, lottery, make, million, newsagent's, pocket, politician, princess, put, run, scientist, see, singer, sit, story, thousand, washing machine, writer, yesterday. lessons.title: Grammar reference and Wordlist - Unit 10
lessons.content: Grammar reference 10.1 Past Simple positive: Regular verbs add -ed in the Past Simple. play -> played, watch -> watched, listen -> listened, clean -> cleaned, invite -> invited. Many common verbs are irregular: go -> went, see -> saw, have -> had. The form is the same for all persons: I, You, He, She, It, We, They listened to music, went to work, had lunch. 10.2 Past Simple questions and negatives: Present do/does -> Past did. What time does he usually get up? What time did he get up yesterday? Questions with question words: Where did you go? Negative: I didn't go shopping. Yes/No questions: Did they play football? Yes, they did. Did you have a good time? No, I didn't. 10.3 Past time expressions: I went to London three years ago, last year, yesterday, in 2016. Wordlist: ago, autumn, bedtime, cabin, call, camping, canoeing, cards, castle, cathedral, choose, clean, clubhouse, coffee shop, crazy, cycling, dancing, date, dress, fishing, ice-skating, interested, invite, leisure, lucky, market, meal, museum, once, orange juice, outside, rain, relax, rugby, sailing, show, sightseeing, skiing, spring, start, summer, tent, tour, tourist, tourist office, villa, volleyball, walking, wedding, windsurfing, winter, zoo.

lessons.title: Practice - It's my birthday!
lessons.content: Practice: It's my birthday! 1 Listen to the conversation. What does the woman want to do? She wants to buy him a present and take him out for a meal. Why is the man not happy? Because he is turning 30 and feels old. 2 Read and complete the conversation with words from the box. A: Hey, isn't it your birthday soon? B: Yeah, next week on the 15th. A: So, what would you like for your birthday? B: I don't know. I don't need anything. A: But I'd like to buy you something. B: That's kind, but I think I'd like to forget my birthday this year. A: What? You don't want any presents! Why not? B: Well, I'm 30 next week, and that feels old. A: Thirty isn't old. Come on! I'd like to take you out for a meal with some friends. You can choose the restaurant. B: OK, then. Thank you. I'd like that. Just don't tell anyone it's my birthday. A: Oh, that's silly! Listen again and check. Practise the conversations. Birthday wishes 3 Listen to three people. It's their birthday soon. Complete the chart. Jill: present - breakfast in bed, evening - watch a film at home. Sammy: present - a new video game, evening - go out for pizza with friends. Zoe: present - some flowers, evening - have a quiet dinner with her family. Talking about you 4 Think about your next birthday. Ask and answer questions about what you'd like. 'What would you like for your birthday?' 'I'd like a new smartphone and some clothes.' 'What would you like to do on your birthday?' 'I'd like to go out for a meal with friends.'

lessons.title: Everyday English - Signs all around
lessons.content: Everyday English: Signs all around. 1 Look at the signs. Where can you see them? 15 signs: Ladies, PRIVATE, OUT OF ORDER, Exit, PULL, SALE, No parking, No entry, PUSH, CLOSED, ENTRANCE, GENTS, QUEUE HERE, Lift, Reserved. 2 Which sign means ...? 1 ENTRANCE - You can go in here. 2 Exit - You can go out here. 3 Reserved - You can't sit here. 4 No parking - You can't park here. 5 OUT OF ORDER - This machine doesn't work. 6 PUSH - Push this door to open it. 7 PULL - Pull this door to open it. 8 GENTS - Men can go to the toilet here. 9 Lift - You can go up or down the floors here. 10 Ladies - Women can go to the toilet here. 11 SALE - You can buy something cheap here. 12 QUEUE HERE - Stand and wait here. 13 CLOSED - Not open. 14 No entry - You can't go in here. 3 Listen to the lines of conversation. Which sign do they go with? 1 OUT OF ORDER, 2 No parking, 3 PUSH, 4 PULL, 5 CLOSED, 6 QUEUE HERE, 7 PRIVATE, 8 No entry. 4 Work with a partner. Write a conversation that goes with a sign. Act it out to the class. Can they identify the correct sign? Go online for more speaking practice.

lessons.title: Grammar reference - would like, some and any, like vs would like
lessons.content: Grammar reference 12.1 would like: We use would like to ask for things. Positive: I'd like a cup of tea. We use 'Would ... like?' to offer things. Question: Would you like some cake? Answers: Yes, please. No, thank you. We use would like, not want, to be polite. I'd like a coffee, please. We can use would like with another verb: Would you like to go out tonight? What would you like to do? 12.2 some and any: We use some in positive sentences: I'd like some ham. There's some cheese. We have some books. We use any in questions: Is there any ham? Do you have any money? Are there any people? We use any in negatives: There isn't any bread. We don't have any friends. There aren't any books. We use some when we offer things or ask for things: Would you like some wine? Can I have some cheese? 12.3 like and would like: We use like (like doing) to talk about things we always like: I like coffee. She likes swimming. We use would like to talk about things we want now or soon: I'd like a coffee. I'd like to go shopping.

I can't answer them. 2 I'm selling my old car and I'm buying a new one. 3 We always get up at 7:00 in the morning and go to bed at 11:00 at night. 4 It was cold, so Tom took off his T-shirt and put on a warm jumper. 5 I usually walk to school, but yesterday I was late so I ran all the way. 6 John's playing tennis with Pete today. lessons.content: Everyday English: What's the matter? 1 What's the matter with the people? Complete the sentences with words in the box: bored, hungry, thirsty, cold, hot, tired, worried, angry, a cold, a headache. 1 She's cold. 2 He's hot. 3 They're hungry. 4 He's tired. 5 They're thirsty. 6 She's bored. 7 He's worried. 8 She's angry. 9 He has a cold. 10 She has a headache. lessons.title: Grammar reference - Present Continuous and Present Simple vs Present Continuous
lessons.content: Grammar reference 13.1 Present Continuous: Positive: I am working. He/She/It is working. You/We/They are working. Negative: I'm not working. He isn't working. You aren't working. Questions with question words: What am I wearing? What are we wearing? What are they wearing? Is he wearing? Is she wearing? Yes/No questions: Are you wearing jeans? Yes, I am. No, I'm not. Is she reading a newspaper? Yes, she is. No, she isn't. 13.2 Present Simple and Present Continuous: We use the Present Simple to talk about actions that are true for all time or a long time: Hans comes from Germany. I love you. My father works in a bank. I get up every day. She doesn't understand French. We use the Present Continuous to talk about actions that last a short time. The actions are happening now: I usually wear jeans, but today I'm wearing a suit. He speaks French very well. He's speaking French to that man. It's raining. They're swimming. We're playing football.

B: hard, a photo, by train, dinner with friends, cards, carefully, a suit, bills online, your homework. play cards, drive carefully, go by train, work hard, have dinner with friends, do your homework, take a photo, pay bills online, wear a suit. Waiter is different (not a family relationship). 3 lovely, fantastic, amazing, awful. Awful is different (negative meaning). 4 trainers, trousers, socks, boots. Trousers is different (not worn on feet). 5 desk, armchair, sofa, laptop. Laptop is different (not furniture). 6 actor, journalist, cooker, builder. Cooker is different (not a person/job). Pronunciation 4 Listen and write the words in the correct box. Two syllables: pilot, hotel, women, married, chocolate, enjoy, shampoo, arrive. 5 Listen and write the words in the correct box. Zambia. Check it 3 Correct the mistakes. 1 He comes from Canada. 2 Where do you live? (correct) 3 I don't want to go out. 4 She is 18 years old. 5 I went to Italy last year. 6 He has a dog and a cat. 7 I can't understand you. 8 What did you do last night? 9 I am going to see a film tonight. 10 What are you going to do this weekend? 4 Choose the correct answer. 1 b some, 2 a there's, 3 b that, 4 a any, 5 a this, 6 b an, 7 b mother's, 8 a English very well, 9 b German car, 10 a I'd like.

lessons.title: Grammar reference - Future plans and Wordlist
lessons.content: Grammar reference 14.1 Future plans: Positive - Present Continuous: I'm going to Europe. You're leaving next week. He's flying on Sunday. Going to: I'm going to see Buckingham Palace. You're going to have a tour of the city. They're going to stay in the Ritz Hotel. Negative - Present Continuous: I'm not living in London. He isn't studying medicine. Going to: I'm not going to travel by train. You aren't going to sleep in a tent. Questions - Present Continuous: Where are you going on holiday? When are you leaving? Where are you staying? Who are you going with? Going to: Where are you going to stay? What are you going to do?
